questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A boat crosses a river from one bank A to another bank B which is opposite. The distance between them is D. The speed of water is $V_W$ and that of boat relative to water is $V_B$. If $V_B = 2V_W$, the time taken by the boat to cross the river directly along AB is $\left(\sin 30^\circ = \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$, $\left(\cos 30^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$
questions.solution:
Let the boat be steered at an angle $\theta$ upstream with respect to the line AB to cross the river directly.

For the boat to move exactly along AB, the component of its velocity parallel to the river flow must cancel the river's velocity $V_W$.

$V_B \sin \theta = V_W$

Given $V_B = 2V_W$, substituting this yields:

$2V_W \sin \theta = V_W \Rightarrow \sin \theta = \dfrac{1}{2} \Rightarrow \theta = 30^\circ$

The net velocity of the boat along the line AB is the component of $V_B$ perpendicular to the river flow:

$V = V_B \cos \theta = V_B \cos 30^\circ = V_B \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$

The time taken to cross the river of width $D$ is:

$t = \dfrac{D}{V} = \dfrac{D}{V_B \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}} = \dfrac{2D}{V_B \sqrt{3}}$

Answer: $\dfrac{2D}{V_B\sqrt{3}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ball is released from height 'h' which makes perfectly elastic collision with ground. The frequency of periodic vibratory motion is (g=acceleration due to gravity)
questions.solution:
Time taken by the ball to fall from height $h$ to the ground is given by $t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}}$.

Since the collision is perfectly elastic, the ball rebounds with the same speed and reaches the same height $h$. The time taken to go up is also $t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}}$.

The total time period of one complete oscillation is $T = 2t = 2\sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}}$.

The frequency of the periodic motion is $f = \dfrac{1}{T} = \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{\dfrac{g}{2h}}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{\dfrac{g}{2h}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A stone falls from the top of a tower of height $100$ m and at the same time another stone is projected vertically upwards from the ground with a velocity $25$ m/s. The two stones meet after
questions.solution:
Let the two stones meet after time $t$.

For the stone falling from the top of the tower:
Displacement downwards, $h_1 = \dfrac{1}{2}gt^2$

For the stone projected upwards from the ground:
Displacement upwards, $h_2 = 25t - \dfrac{1}{2}gt^2$

When the two stones meet, the sum of their displacements is equal to the height of the tower.
$h_1 + h_2 = 100$

$\dfrac{1}{2}gt^2 + 25t - \dfrac{1}{2}gt^2 = 100$

$25t = 100$

$t = 4$ s

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Spherical insulating ball and a spherical metallic ball of same size and mass are dropped from the same height. Choose the correct statement out of the following {Assume negligible air friction}
options: Time taken by them to reach the earth's surface will be independent of the properties of their materials.
Insulating ball will reach the earth's surface earlier than the metal ball.
Both will reach the earth's surface simultaneously.
Metal ball will reach the earth's surface earlier than the insulating ball.
questions.solution:
As the metallic ball falls through the Earth's magnetic field, it cuts the magnetic field lines, which induces an electromotive force (EMF) in it.

Since the ball is a conductor, this induced EMF generates eddy currents within the metallic ball.

According to Lenz's law, these eddy currents oppose the motion that causes them, creating an upward magnetic retarding force.

As a result, the net downward acceleration of the metallic ball becomes less than the acceleration due to gravity $g$.

The insulating ball is a non-conductor, so no eddy currents are induced in it. It falls with the full acceleration $g$.

Because the insulating ball has a greater downward acceleration, it will reach the Earth's surface earlier than the metallic ball.

Answer: Insulating ball will reach the earth's surface earlier than the metal ball.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The velocity time graph of a body moving in a straight line is shown in a figure. The ratio of displacement to distance travelled by the body in time $0$ to $10$ s is
questions.solution:
Displacement is the algebraic sum of the areas under the velocity-time graph, and distance is the sum of their absolute values.

Calculating the areas for each time interval:
Area for $0$ to $2$ s: $A_1 = 8 \times 2 = 16$ m
Area for $2$ to $4$ s: $A_2 = -4 \times 2 = -8$ m
Area for $4$ to $8$ s: $A_3 = 4 \times 4 = 16$ m
Area for $8$ to $10$ s: $A_4 = -4 \times 2 = -8$ m

Total displacement $= A_1 + A_2 + A_3 + A_4 = 16 - 8 + 16 - 8 = 16$ m

Total distance $= |A_1| + |A_2| + |A_3| + |A_4| = 16 + 8 + 16 + 8 = 48$ m

Ratio of displacement to distance $= \dfrac{16}{48} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Thus, the required ratio is $1:3$.

Answer: $1:3$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A car passes three points A, B and C at $3$ m/s, $6$ m/s and $9$ m/s respectively in a straight line with uniform acceleration. If distance $AB = 60$ m then find the distance BC.
questions.solution:
Using the equation of motion $v^2 - u^2 = 2as$ for the interval AB:

$v_B^2 - v_A^2 = 2a(AB)$

$6^2 - 3^2 = 2a(60)$

$36 - 9 = 120a$

$27 = 120a \Rightarrow a = \dfrac{27}{120} = \dfrac{9}{40}$ m/s$^2$

Applying the same equation for the interval BC:

$v_C^2 - v_B^2 = 2a(BC)$

$9^2 - 6^2 = 2 \times \dfrac{9}{40} \times BC$

$81 - 36 = \dfrac{9}{20} \times BC$

$45 = \dfrac{9}{20} \times BC$

$BC = \dfrac{45 \times 20}{9} = 100$ m

Answer: $100$ m

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If a ball is thrown vertically upwards with speed ' $u$ ', the distance covered by it during the last ' $t$ ' second of its ascent is ( $g=$ acceleration due to gravity)
questions.solution:
Distance during last t seconds of ascent

A ball thrown upward with initial speed $u$ reaches its peak when final velocity is zero. The distance covered in the last $t$ seconds of ascent equals the distance it would fall from rest in time $t$.

For free fall from rest: initial velocity $u' = 0$, acceleration $g$, time $t$.

$s = u't + \frac{1}{2}gt^2$

Substituting $u' = 0$:

$s = \frac{1}{2}gt^2$

The correct option is D.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A car moving at a speed ' $V$ ' is stopped in a certain distance when the breaks produce a deceleration 'a'. If the speed of the car is 'nv', what must be the deceleration of the car to stop it in the same distance and in the same time?
questions.solution:
A car stops from speed \(v\) under deceleration \(a\).
Using
\(v=a t \quad \text { and } \quad s=\frac{1}{2} v t\)
(the distance-time relations during uniform deceleration).
Now the new speed is \(n v\).
Let required deceleration be \(\boldsymbol{A}\).
For same stopping time:
\(n v=A t \quad \Rightarrow \quad A=n a\)
For same stopping distance:
\(s=\frac{1}{2} v t=\frac{1}{2}(n v) t^{\prime}\)
But time is same, so:
\(\frac{1}{2} v t=\frac{1}{2} n v t \cdot \frac{a}{A}\)
Or use direct formula for distance:
\(\frac{v^2}{2 a}=\frac{(n v)^2}{2 A}\)
Thus,
\(\frac{v^2}{a}=\frac{n^2 v^2}{A} \Rightarrow A=n^2 a .\)
\(n^2 a\)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A boy throws a ball vertically upwards from a bridge with velocity $5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. It strikes water surface after 2 s . The height of the bridge is $\left(\right.$ Take $\left.g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2\right)$
questions.solution:
The height of the bridge is determined using kinematic equations with upward defined as positive. The ball's initial velocity is $u = +5\,\text{m/s}$, the time until impact is $t = 2\,\text{s}$, and acceleration due to gravity is $a = -10\,\text{m/s}^2$.

The displacement equation $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ applies, where $s = -h$ represents the downward displacement from the bridge to the water surface. Substituting the values:

$-h = (5)(2) + \frac{1}{2}(-10)(2)^2$
$= 10 - 20$
$= -10$

Solving yields $h = 10\,\text{m}$.

The height of the bridge is 10 meters.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The acceleration (a) - time (T) graph for the body starting from rest is given below. The maximum speed of the body is
questions.solution:
The area under the acceleration–time graph represents the change in velocity.

Given initial velocity $u = 0 \, \text{m/s}$, the maximum speed occurs at $t = 10 \, \text{s}$ since acceleration is positive throughout.

The graph forms a right triangle from $t = 0$ to $t = 10$ seconds, with base $10 \, \text{s}$ and height $8 \, \text{m/s}^2$.
The area is $\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 8 = 40 \, \text{m/s}$.

Thus, $v_\text{max} = 40 \, \text{m/s}$.

The correct option is A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: At any time ' $t$ ', the co-ordinates of moving particle are $x=a t^2$ and $\mathrm{y}=\mathrm{bt}^2$. The speed of the particle is
questions.solution:
The position of the particle at time $t$ is defined by $x = at^2$ and $y = bt^2$. Differentiating both coordinates with respect to time, the velocity components are $v_x = 2at$ and $v_y = 2bt$.

The speed is the magnitude of the velocity vector:

$v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{(2at)^2 + (2bt)^2} = \sqrt{4a^2t^2 + 4b^2t^2} = \sqrt{4t^2(a^2 + b^2)} = 2t\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}$.

This result corresponds to option A.

$\boxed{\text{A}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body starts from rest and moves with a uniform acceleration. The ratio of the distance covered by the body in the $\mathrm{n}^{\text {th }}$ second of its motion to the total distance travelled in n second is
questions.solution:
A body starts from rest with uniform acceleration of magnitude $a$. The distance covered in the $\mathrm{n}^{\text{th}}$ second is $S_n^{\text{th}} = u + \frac{a}{2}(2n - 1)$. With initial velocity $u = 0$, this becomes $S_n^{\text{th}} = \frac{a}{2}(2n - 1)$.

The total distance traveled in $n$ seconds is $S_n = \frac{1}{2}an^2$.

The ratio is then $\frac{S_n^{\text{th}}}{S_n} = \frac{\frac{a}{2}(2n - 1)}{\frac{1}{2}an^2} = \frac{2n - 1}{n^2}$, which simplifies to $\frac{2}{n} - \frac{1}{n^2}$.

The correct option is C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The velocity time graph of a body moving in a straight line is shown in figure. The ratio of displacement to distance travelled by the body in time 0 to 8 s is
questions.solution:
The displacement is the net area under the velocity-time graph, while distance is the total area taken as positive.

From $t = 0$ to $2$ s: displacement $+6$ m, distance $6$ m.
From $t = 2$ to $3$ s: displacement $-2$ m, distance $2$ m.
The remaining segments follow similarly, yielding displacements of $+4$, $-2$, and $+4$ m, with distances of $4$, $2$, and $4$ m respectively.

The total displacement is $6 - 2 + 4 - 2 + 4 = 10$ m.
The total distance is $6 + 2 + 4 + 2 + 4 = 18$ m.

The ratio simplifies to $10:18 = 5:9$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two bodies A and B move in same straight line starting from same position. Body A moves with constant velocity 'u' and body B moves with constant acceleration ' $a$ '. When their velocities become equal, the distance between them is
questions.solution:
Define $x=0$ as the initial position at $t=0$. Body A moves with constant velocity $v_A = u$, so its position is $x_A = u t$. Body B accelerates from rest with constant acceleration $a$, giving velocity $v_B = a t$ and position $x_B = \frac{1}{2} a t^2$.

Equate their velocities to find when they are equal: $u = a t$, so $t = \frac{u}{a}$.

At this time, $x_A = u \cdot \frac{u}{a} = \frac{u^2}{a}$ and $x_B = \frac{1}{2} a \left( \frac{u}{a} \right)^2 = \frac{u^2}{2a}$. The distance between them is the absolute difference, which simplifies to $D = \left| \frac{u^2}{a} - \frac{u^2}{2a} \right| = \frac{u^2}{2a}$.

The final answer is $\boxed{\text{D}}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body travelling with uniform acceleration crosses two points A and B with velocities $20 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ and $30 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ respectively. The speed of the body at mid point of A and B is (nearly)
questions.solution:
Let the acceleration of the body be ' $a$ ' and the distance between points A and B be ' d '. $\begin{aligned} & \therefore \quad \mathrm{v}^2-\mathrm{u}^2=2 \mathrm{ad} \quad \ldots\left(\text { from } \mathrm{v}^2=\mathrm{u}^2+2 \mathrm{as}\right) \\ & \mathrm{ad}=\frac{\mathrm{v}^2-\mathrm{u}^2}{2}=\frac{(30)^2-(20)^2}{2} \\ &=250 \end{aligned}$
When the body is at the mid-point of $A B$, then speed of the body is $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{v}_1^2-(20)^2=2 \mathrm{a}\left(\frac{\mathrm{~d}}{2}\right) \\ & \mathrm{v}_1^2-400=\mathrm{ad} \\ & \mathrm{v}_1=\sqrt{650} \\ & \mathrm{v}_1=25.5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The co-ordinates of a moving particle at any time ' t ' are given by $x=\alpha \mathrm{t}^3$ and $y=\beta \mathrm{t}^3$ where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are constants. The speed of the particle at time ' $t$ ' is given by
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & X=\alpha t^3 \hat{i}+\beta t^3 \hat{j} \\ & \begin{aligned} V=\frac{d X}{d t}=3 \alpha t^2 \hat{i} & +3 \beta t^2 \hat{j} \\ \text { Magnitude of } V & =\sqrt{\left(3 \alpha t^2\right)^2+\left(3 \beta t^2\right)^2} \\ & =\sqrt{9 \alpha^2 t^4+9 \beta^2 t^4} \\ & =\sqrt{9 t^4\left(\alpha^2+\beta^2\right)} \\ & =3 t^2 \sqrt{\alpha^2+\beta^2}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ball is released from the top of a tower of height H m. It takes T second to reach the ground. The height of the ball from the ground after $\frac{T}{4}$ second is
questions.solution:
Let the body be at $x$ from the top after $\frac{t}{4} \mathrm{~s}$. $\mathrm{x}=\mathrm{ut}+\frac{1}{2} a \mathrm{t}^2=\frac{1}{2} a \mathrm{t}^2\ldots(\because u=0)\therefore \quad x=\frac{1}{2} g\left(\frac{\mathrm{t}}{4}\right)^2=\frac{g t^2}{32} \Rightarrow 32 \mathrm{x}=\mathrm{gt}^2...(i)\mathrm{H}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{gt}^2 \Rightarrow 2 \mathrm{H}=\mathrm{gt}^2...(ii)$
From (i) and (ii), we get $2 \mathrm{H}=32 \mathrm{x} \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=\frac{2 \mathrm{H}}{32}\therefore \quad$ Height of the body from the ground $=\mathrm{H}-\frac{2 \mathrm{H}}{32}=\frac{15 \mathrm{H}}{16}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two cars start from a point at the same time in a straight line and their positions are represented by $\mathrm{x}_1(\mathrm{t})=\mathrm{at}+\mathrm{bt}^2$ and $\mathrm{x}_2(\mathrm{t})=\mathrm{Ft}-\mathrm{t}^2$. At what time do the cars have the same velocity?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \text { Velocity } v=\frac{d x}{d t} \\
\therefore \quad & v_P=\frac{d x_P}{d t}=a+2 b t \\
& v_Q=\frac{d x_Q}{d t}=F-2 t \\
& a v_P=v_Q ...(given)\\
& a+2 b t=F-2 t \\
\therefore \quad & (2+2 b) t=F-a \Rightarrow t=\frac{F-a}{2(1+b)}
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A bullet is fired on a target with velocity V. Its velocity decreases from $v$ to $v / 2$. When it penetrates 30 cm in a target. Through what thickness it will penetrate further in the target before coming to rest?
questions.solution:
When the velocity of the bullet changes from V to $\frac{\mathrm{V}}{2}$ the distance travelled by the bullet is 30 cm . Using $3^{\text {rd }}$ kinematic equation, $\begin{aligned} & v^2=u^2+2 a s \\ & \left(\frac{V}{2}\right)^2=V^2+2 a(30) \\ & \frac{V^2}{4}=V^2+60 a \\ & \frac{-3 V^2}{4}=60 a \\ & a=\frac{-V^2}{80} \end{aligned}$
Further, when a bullet penetrates. it comes to rest. So, the final velocity of the bullet becomes zero. Using the relation, $v^2=u^2+2 \mathrm{as}\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{v}^2=\mathrm{u}^2+2 \mathrm{as} \\ & 0=\left(\frac{\mathrm{V}}{2}\right)^2+2\left(-\frac{\mathrm{V}^2}{80}\right) \mathrm{s} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{V}^2}{4}=\left(\frac{\mathrm{V}^2}{40}\right) \mathrm{s} \\ & \mathrm{s}=\frac{40}{4}=10 \mathrm{~cm}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: For the velocity-time graph shown in the figure below, the distance covered by the body in last two second of its motion is ' $\mathrm{S}_1$ '. What is the ratio of ' $S_1$ ' to the total distance covered by it
questions.solution:
Distance covered = Area enclosed by velocity-time graph.
Total distance covered in 6 seconds,
$S=\frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 10+2 \times 10+\frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 10=40 m$

Distance covered in last two seconds,
$\begin{aligned}
& S^{\prime}=\frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 10=10 \mathrm{~m} \\
& \therefore \text { Fraction of distance }=\frac{S^{\prime}}{S}=\frac{10}{40}=\frac{1}{4}
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A vehicle runs on a straight road of length ' L '. It travels half the distance with speed V and the remaining distance with speed $\frac{\mathrm{V}}{3}$. Its average speed is
questions.solution: Average velocity, $\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{avg}}=\frac{2 \mathrm{~V}_1 \mathrm{~V}_2}{\mathrm{~V}_1+\mathrm{V}_2}$ Given $\mathrm{V}_1=\mathrm{V}$ and $\mathrm{V}_2=\frac{\mathrm{V}}{3}\therefore \quad \mathrm{V}_{\text {avg }}=\frac{2 \times \mathrm{V} \times \frac{\mathrm{V}}{3}}{\mathrm{~V}+\frac{\mathrm{V}}{3}}=\frac{2 \mathrm{~V}^2}{3} \times \frac{3}{4 \mathrm{~V}}=\frac{\mathrm{V}}{2}$

questions.q:
The following figures show the variation of displacement with time of a particular object. (a)
(b)
(c)
(d)

Figure (b) and (c) show object at rest and object moving with uniform velocity in negative $x$ direction respectively.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A velocity - time graph of a body is shown below. The distance covered by the body from 6 second to 9 second is
questions.solution:
Given Graph: The graph consists of straight lines, and the distance is the area under the velocitytime curve.
Split the graph from $t=6$ to $t=9$ : - $t=6$ to $t=8$ : Rectangle with base 2 s and height $30 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$, $\text {Area }=\text { Base } \times \text { Height }=2 \times 30=60 \mathrm{~m}$ - $t=8$ to $t=9$ : Triangle with base 1 s and height $10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$, $\text {Area }=\frac{1}{2} \times \text { Base } \times \text { Height }=\frac{1}{2} \times 1 \times 10=5 \mathrm{~m}$
Total Distance: $\text {Total Distance }=60+5=65 \mathrm{~m}$
Answer: 65 m, closest to Option 3: 82.5 m (if rounded incorrectly in solution).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A driver applies the brakes on seeing the red traffic signal 400 m ahead. At the time of applying brakes, the vehicle was moving with $15 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ and retarding at $0.3 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$. The distance of the vehicle from the traffic light one minute after application of brakes is
questions.solution:
After applying the brakes, the vehicle stops after time t , $\mathrm{t}=\left(\frac{\mathrm{v}-\mathrm{u}}{\mathrm{a}}\right)=\left(\frac{0-15}{-0.3}\right)=50 \text { seconds }$ i.e. vehicle stops before one minute. ⇒ Displacement will only occur for 50 seconds. $\therefore \quad$ Displacement is given by $\mathrm{s}=\mathrm{ut}+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{at}^2\therefore \quad \mathrm{s}=15 \times 50+\frac{1}{2} \times(-0.3) \times(50)^2\ldots .(\because \mathrm{a}$ is the retardation in vehicle) $\mathrm{s}=375 \mathrm{~m}$
Distance from traffic light $=400-375=25 \mathrm{~m}$

questions.solution:

$\mathrm{V}=2 \mathrm{at}-3 \mathrm{bt} \mathrm{t}^2$

$A=2 a-6 b t$

\therefore \quad \mathrm{t} & =\frac{2 \mathrm{a}}{6 \mathrm{~b}}=\frac{\mathrm{a}}{3 \mathrm{~b}} &

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two bodies 'A' an 'B' start from the same point at the same instant and move along a straight line. Body 'A' moves with uniform acceleration ' $a$ ' and body ' $B$ ' moves with uniform velocity ' $V$ '. They meet after time ' $t$ '. The value of ' $t$ ' is
questions.solution:
At point $A$,
$\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{A}}=\mathrm{ut}+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{at}^2\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{A}}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{at}^2$
At point $B$,
$\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{B}}=\mathrm{vt}\therefore \quad$ At the point where they meet,
$\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{A}}=\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{B}}\frac{1}{2} a t^2=v tt=\frac{2 v}{a}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A small steel ball is dropped from a height of $1.5 \mathrm{~m}$ into a glycerine jar. The ball reaches the bottom of the jar 1.5 second after it was dropped. If the retardation is $2.66 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$, the height of the glycerine in the jar is about (acceleration due to gravity $g=9.8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ )
questions.solution:
The velocity of the ball after it has been dropped from height till it reaches the glycerine surface is
$\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{i}}^2=0+2 \mathrm{gh} \quad \quad \ldots .\left(\because \mathrm{v}^2-\mathrm{u}^2=2 \mathrm{gh}\right)v_i^2=2 \times 9.8 \times 1.5v_i^2=29.4$
The velocity of the ball after it enters glycerine is $v_f^2=v_i^2-2 g h0=29.4-(2 \times 2.66 \times h)\therefore \quad \mathrm{h}=\frac{29.4}{2 \times 2.66}=5.5 \mathrm{~m}$

questions.q: A body is released from the top of a tower ' $\mathrm{H}$ ' metre high. It takes $t$ second to reach the ground. The height of the body $\frac{t}{2}$ second after release is
questions.solution:
Let the body be at $\mathrm{x}$ from the top after $\frac{\mathrm{t}}{2} \mathrm{~s}$.
$\begin{aligned}
\therefore \quad \mathrm{x} & =\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~g} \frac{\mathrm{t}^2}{4}=\frac{\mathrm{gt}^2}{8}.... (i) \\
\mathrm{H} & =\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{gt}^2 .... (ii)
\end{aligned}$
Eliminating $\mathrm{t}$ from (i) and (ii), we get $\frac{8 \mathrm{x}}{\mathrm{g}}=\frac{2 \mathrm{H}}{\mathrm{g}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=\frac{\mathrm{H}}{4}\therefore \quad$ Height of the body from the ground $=\mathrm{H}-\frac{\mathrm{H}}{4}=\frac{3 \mathrm{H}}{4}$ metres

questions.q: A vehicle of mass 'M' is moving with momentum 'P' on a rough horizontal road. The coefficient of friction between the tyres and the horizontal road is '$\mu$'. The stopping distance is (g $=$ acceleration due to gravity)
questions.solution: Initial velocity $\mathrm{u}=\frac{\mathrm{p}}{\mathrm{m}}$ Final velocity $\mathrm{v}=0$ (as the vehicle must stop) Force of friction $=\mu \mathrm{mg}$ (where $\mathrm{g}$ is acceleration due to gravity) Acceleration due to friction $=-\frac{\mu \mathrm{mg}}{\mathrm{m}}=-\mu \mathrm{g}$ (-ve sign shows that it is retardation ) Using the kinematic expression \mathrm{v}^{2}=\mathrm{u}^{2}=2 \mathrm{as} and inserting various values we get stopping distance $s$ \begin{array}{l} (0)^{2}-\frac{\mathrm{p}^{2}}{\mathrm{~m}^{2}}=2(-\mu \mathrm{g}) \mathrm{s} \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{s}=\frac{\mathrm{p}^{2}}{2 \mu^{2} \mu \mathrm{g}} \end{array}

\(\mathrm{v}^{2}=\mathrm{u}^{2}-2 \mathrm{as}\)
\(\therefore \mathrm{a} \frac{u^{2}}{2 \mathrm{~s}}=\frac{150 \times 150}{36 \times 36 \times 2 \times 5} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}\)
Next \(\mathrm{s}=\frac{u^{2}}{2 a}=\frac{45000}{60 \times 60} \times \frac{45000}{60 \times 60} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{36 \times 36}{150 \times 15}\)
\(=45 \mathrm{~m}\)
